props.title: September Issue

sections.content: **The September Issue** (2009) revolutionized fashion documentary filmmaking by taking viewers behind Vogue magazine's fortress-like walls. Director R.J. Cutler captured the fascinating power dynamic between ice queen editor Anna Wintour and creative director Grace Coddington during the production of Vogue's biggest annual issue. The film arrived perfectly timed after **The Devil Wears Prada** (2006) had mythologized Wintour's persona, but showed the real woman's shrewd business instincts and lightning-fast decision-making that kept Vogue at fashion's pinnacle.

sections.content: Fashion documentaries evolved significantly in the 2010s, moving beyond just glamour to examine the industry's darker sides. **The True Cost** (2015) exposed fast fashion's environmental and human toll, while **McQueen** (2018) painted a haunting portrait of a creative genius's tragic trajectory. These films pulled back fashion's glossy curtain to reveal the commercial pressures, psychological costs, and ethical challenges facing the industry.

The intersection of art and commerce features prominently in modern fashion docs. **Iris** (2014) celebrates style icon Iris Apfel's creative independence, while **Fresh Dressed** (2015) explores how hip-hop revolutionized fashion. **House of Z** (2017) chronicles Zac Posen's meteoric rise and humbling comeback, revealing fashion's ruthless business realities. sections.content: Recent fashion documentaries increasingly focus on industry transformation and next-generation voices. **Martin Margiela: In His Own Words** (2019) finally revealed the famously private designer's philosophy, while **Wonder Boy** (2019) showed Olivier Rousteing's personal journey as Balmain's young creative director. These films capture fashion's shift toward transparency, inclusivity, and digital innovation.
